(Capacity: 13,819) | champion = [[2022–23 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 regular season champions]] | tourney = [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2022–23 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 NCAA Division I season]]. The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] were led by fourth-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]], and they played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. Guard/forward [[Jaime Jaquez Jr.]] was named a second-team [[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].{{cite news|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|title=Sporting News 2022-23 college basketball All-America team|date=March 7, 2023|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2022-23-college-basketball-all-america-team/ynhqsffrvax9novxmglr2fgo|work=[[Sporting News]]|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]], and received first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors along with guard [[Tyger Campbell]]. Guard [[Jaylen Clark]] was named to the second team and was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]]. He was placed on the conference's all-defensive team along with forward [[Adem Bona]], who was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]]. [[Amari Bailey]] joined Bona on the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team, and Cronin was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Coach of the Year|Pac-12 Coach of the Year]].{{cite press release|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|date=March 7, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2023/3/7/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance.aspx|access-date=March 7, 2023}} UCLA lost five players who were major contributors from [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|their previous year's squad]] that went 27–8.{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA's Jaime Jaquez Jr. named Pac-12 Player of the Year|date=March 7, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/07/uclas-jaime-jaquez-jr-named-pac-12-player-of-the-year/|access-date=March 8, 2023}} However, the Bruins were also the only team in the [[Power Five conferences|power conferences]] whose roster consisted entirely of players who began their college careers at that school.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/how-transfer-portal-nil-reshaping-college-basketball-recruiting-has-dropped-value-of-high-school-prospects/ |title=How transfer portal, NIL reshaping college basketball recruiting has dropped value of high school prospects |first=Matt |last=Norlander |website=CBSSports.com |date=July 8, 2023 |access-date=July 21, 2023}} With a 60–56 win over [[2022–23 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]] on February 26, 2023, the Bruins clinched their first Pac-12 regular season championship since [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]].{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA defeats Colorado to clinch its first Pac-12 championship in a decade|date=February 26, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-26/ucla-mens-basketball-pac-12-title-colorado-recap|access-date=February 27, 2023}} UCLA ended the regular season with an 82–73 win over No. 8 [[2022–23 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], extending their home winning streak to 25 games, the longest active streak in the nation. They won the conference by four games and finished the season undefeated at home for the first time since [[2006–07 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2006–07]].{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA beats Arizona in Senior Night sendoff, but Jaylen Clark leaves with injury|date=March 4, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-04/ucla-defeats-arizona-college-basketball-recap|access-date=March 5, 2023}} Clark left the game with a lower leg injury, and was ruled out for the [[2023 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]].{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Sources: UCLA's Jaylen Clark (Achilles) out for rest of season|date=March 9, 2023|work=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35813516/sources-ucla-jaylen-clark-achilles-remainder-season|access-date=March 12, 2023}} The top-seeded Bruins advanced to the tournament finals before losing 61–59 to No. 2-seed Arizona, ending their 12-game winning streak. UCLA played without its top two defenders,{{cite web|first=Billy|last=Witz|title=Seedings for N.C.A.A. Men's Tournament Show Wide-Open Field|date=March 12, 2023|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/12/sports/ncaabasketball/ncaa-tournament-seedings.html|access-date=March 14, 2023}} as Bona also missed the game with an injured left shoulder,{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA falls to Arizona in Pac-12 title game, hurting chances for a No. 1 NCAA seed|date=March 11, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-11/ucla-mens-basketball-loses-to-arizona-pac-12-recap|access-date=March 12, 2023}} which he suffered in the semifinals against [[2022–23 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]].{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Grosbard|title=Undersized UCLA loses thrilling Pac-12 Tournament title game to Arizona|date=March 11, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/11/undersized-ucla-loses-thrilling-pac-12-championship-game-to-arizona/|access-date=March 12, 2023}} The Bruins, who were vying for a No. 1 seed in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], received a No. 2 seed in the West Region. It was their highest seeding since they were placed No. 1 in [[2007–08 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008]]. However, Clark was ruled out for the season.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=March Madness: UCLA's seniors ready for their last chance to dance|date=March 12, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-12/ucla-basketball-ncaa-tournament-seeded-second-west-regional|access-date=March 12, 2023}} Bona was cleared to return in their opener, but he did not play in the 86–53 rout over No. 15-seed [[2022–23 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]].{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA dodges upset trend, opens NCAA tournament with rout of UNC Asheville|date=March 16, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-16/ucla-vs-unc-asheville-ncaa-tournament-recap|access-date=March 18, 2023}} He played in the second round against [[2022–23 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]], which UCLA won to advance to the Sweet Sixteen for the third straight season.{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=UCLA edges Northwestern to advance to 3rd straight Sweet Sixteen|date=March 18, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/18/ucla-edges-northwestern-to-advance-to-third-straight-sweet-sixteen/|access-date=March 20, 2023}} The Bruins were eliminated 79–76 by third-seeded [[2022–23 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]]. UCLA led by 13 points at halftime, but were down by 10 in the second half with 2:40 remaining. They outscored the Bulldogs 14–3, culminating with a [[three-point field goal]] by Bailey to take a one-point lead. However, Gonzaga's [[Julian Strawther]] made a {{convert|35|ft|adj=on}} basket with six seconds remaining, and they held on for the win. Bona sat out the game due to his shoulder.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jubilation turns into heartbreak as UCLA loses to Gonzaga again in NCAA tournament|date=March 23, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-23/ucla-basketball-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament-sweet-16-recap|access-date=March 24, 2023}} The game was rematch of the schools' Final Four matchup from [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2021]], also won by the Bulldogs, on a {{convert|40|ft|adj=on}} [[buzzer beater]] by [[Jalen Suggs]] to end the game.{{cite web|title=Gonzaga beats UCLA 79-76 in Sweet 16 on Strawther's shot|date=March 24, 2023|work=ESPN|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401522186|access-date=March 24, 2023}}{{cite Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-23/ucla-gonzaga-march-madness-sweet-16-ncaa-tournament|access-date=March 24, 2023}} It was the Bruins' third consecutive loss to the
